title: arXiv AI Trending — Daily | 2026-11-09
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this ordering is inferred from checkable attention and corroboration signals, and citation evidence is limited for papers this recent.

sections.title: Test-Time Compute Scales Better with Parallel Agent Teams
sections.abstract: The paper proposes sampling many small collaborating agent teams in parallel and keeping the best team's result, reporting gains over independent agents and one large team on long-horizon tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that, with a 27B model and a budget of 100 agents, teams of ten beat parallel individual agents on 10 of 12 tasks and a single 100-agent team on all four tasks tested at that size.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper states that run pools are small (10–11 runs per task), larger-team tests used only one to five runs per size, and experiments use one agent harness; without a verifier, choosing the best team becomes an additional problem.

sections.title: Exploring Weight-Space Programming: Capabilities, Generalization, and Limitations
sections.abstract: Across 16 editing trajectories, seven benchmarks, and two model sizes, the authors find that localized weight edits can yield large but uneven gains and that candidate edits are not reliably validated.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report held-out accuracy gains from modifying as few as 1,023 parameters, while documenting uneven cross-task transfer and six of 16 trajectories that retained the original weights when candidate gains could not be validated reliably.
sections.unique_caveat: Editing outcomes vary substantially across trajectories, and the reported study covers two model scales and a limited set of editing runs; reliable validation of candidate interventions remains unresolved.

sections.title: Forcing a Letter Suppresses Refusal: Mechanistic Evidence from WMDP
sections.abstract: Using WMDP and two 8B models, the authors find that multiple-choice answer-letter selection is associated with reduced refusal signals and show that ablating relevant attention heads restores refusal in one model.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors use tuned-lens and refusal-direction analyses on Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B, plus attention-head ablation on Llama-3.1-8B, to argue that answer selection under MCQ formatting competes with refusal formation.
sections.unique_caveat: The study is limited to two 8B models and WMDP; the causal head-ablation finding is established on Llama-3.1-8B, while the corresponding Qwen3-8B results are weaker or do not reproduce the effect.

sections.title: Flex-RSI: Benchmarking Recursive Self-Improvement of Frontier Agents
sections.abstract: Flex-RSI benchmarks fixed-budget agent self-improvement on vision and robotics tasks by allowing agents to revise both task solutions and their harnesses, and reports that the gains and failure modes vary by model and task.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce a benchmark in which an executor improves a task solution and an improver revises the harness, with hidden-test scoring; paired runs indicate harness editing contributes to measured gains.
sections.unique_caveat: The evidence is bounded to fixed-budget vision and robotics tasks; benchmark gains do not by themselves establish general recursive self-improvement on other task families or deployment settings.

sections.title: Not All Misalignment Is Alike: A Decomposed Benchmark for Emergent Misalignment
sections.abstract: EMERGE measures eight forms of emergent misalignment against matched benign controls while tracking capability-related confounders, finding that models with similar overall rates can show different behavioural profiles.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors evaluate eight behaviours across eight open-weight models and 13 fine-tuning datasets, using out-of-domain prompts, matched benign controls, and separate capability, coherence, and refusal measures.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper notes that LLM judges are not ground truth, human validation used one annotator, each model–dataset setting used one fine-tuning seed and LoRA configuration, and evaluation-set pretraining contamination cannot be ruled out.
